# core/num.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/num.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Parsing integers from bytes and formatting them as text.

Parsing reads a span `from..to` of a byte string, so a caller that has
split a line need not copy the pieces. Every parser rejects an empty span,
a byte that is not a digit, and a value that does not fit its type.

What is proved: a parser returns `Some` only for a non-empty run of digits
(spec fns `all_digits`, `all_hex`), and then the value the digits denote
(`bdec`, `bhex`, and `dec_signed` for a leading `-`), so a parser never
overflows. Formatting appends only digits (and padding or a sign) and
keeps what was there. Not proved: that `fmt_u64` writes the digits of `x`
in particular; it writes a `Vec[u8]` and `bdec` reads `Bytes`, so the tests
check that formatting and parsing are inverse instead. Narrower integers
format through `fmt_u64(t, cast[u64](x))`: widening needs no proof.

`import "core/num.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md).

## Functions

### `min_u64`

```bastio
fn min_u64(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64
  ensures result <= a && result <= b && (result == a || result == b)
```

The smaller of `a` and `b`.

Example:

```bastio
let n = min_u64(4096, 100);
let m = max_u64(4096, 100);
assert n <= 100 && m >= 4096;
if n != 100 || m != 4096 { return 1; }
```

### `max_u64`

```bastio
fn max_u64(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64
  ensures result >= a && result >= b && (result == a || result == b)
```

The larger of `a` and `b`.

### `checked_add_u64`

```bastio
fn checked_add_u64(a: u64, b: u64) -> Option[u64]
  ensures (result is Option::Some) == (a + b <= 18446744073709551615)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some == a + b
```

`a + b`, or `None` when it does not fit a `u64`.

Example:

```bastio
let s = checked_add_u64(18446744073709551614, 1);
let t = checked_add_u64(18446744073709551615, 1);
assert s is Option::Some && t is Option::None;   // proved, both ways
let d = checked_sub_u64(3, 5);                   // would go below 0
let m = checked_mul_u64(4294967296, 4294967296); // 2^64
let ok = opt_or[u64](s, 0) == 18446744073709551615 && d is Option::None && m is Option::None
  && opt_or[u64](checked_mul_u64(4096, 512), 0) == 2097152 && opt_or[u64](checked_sub_u64(5, 3), 9) == 2;
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `checked_sub_u64`

```bastio
fn checked_sub_u64(a: u64, b: u64) -> Option[u64]
  ensures (result is Option::Some) == (b <= a)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some == a - b
```

`a - b`, or `None` when `b` is larger.

### `checked_mul_u64`

```bastio
fn checked_mul_u64(a: u64, b: u64) -> Option[u64]
  ensures (result is Option::Some) == (a * b <= 18446744073709551615)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some == a * b
```

`a * b`, or `None` when it does not fit a `u64`.

### `sat_add_u64`

```bastio
fn sat_add_u64(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64
  ensures a + b <= 18446744073709551615 ==> result == a + b
  ensures a + b > 18446744073709551615 ==> result == 18446744073709551615
```

`a + b`, or the largest `u64` when it does not fit.

Example:

```bastio
let a = sat_add_u64(18446744073709551000, 1000);
let b = sat_sub_u64(3, 5);
assert a == 18446744073709551615 && b == 0;
```

### `sat_sub_u64`

```bastio
fn sat_sub_u64(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64
  ensures b <= a ==> result == a - b
  ensures b > a ==> result == 0
```

`a - b`, or 0 when `b` is larger.

### `div_ceil_u64`

```bastio
fn div_ceil_u64(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64
  requires 0 < b
  ensures a % b == 0 ==> result == a / b
  ensures a % b != 0 ==> result == a / b + 1
  ensures a <= result * b && result * b < a + b
```

`a / b` rounded up: how many blocks of `b` hold `a` units.

Example:

```bastio
let pages = div_ceil_u64(10000, 4096);   // 3 pages hold 10000 bytes
let exact = div_ceil_u64(8192, 4096);
assert pages == 3 && exact == 2;
```

### `align_down_u64`

```bastio
fn align_down_u64(x: u64, a: u64) -> u64
  requires 0 < a
  ensures result == x / a * a
  ensures result <= x && x - result < a
```

`x` rounded down to a multiple of `a` (a page or block size, say).

Example:

```bastio
let lo = align_down_u64(10000, 4096);
let hi = align_up_u64(10000, 4096);
assert lo == 8192 && hi == 12288;
let same = align_up_u64(8192, 4096);   // already aligned
assert same == 8192;
```

### `align_up_u64`

```bastio
fn align_up_u64(x: u64, a: u64) -> u64
  requires 0 < a && x <= 18446744073709551615 - (a - 1)
  ensures x % a == 0 ==> result == x
  ensures x % a != 0 ==> result == (x / a + 1) * a
  ensures x <= result && result - x < a
```

`x` rounded up to a multiple of `a`. The caller shows that it fits: for
an address from user space, check `x <= limit` first.

### `is_digit`

```bastio
fn is_digit(c: u8) -> bool
  ensures result == is_digit_spec(c)
```

An ASCII decimal digit, `0` to `9`.

Example:

```bastio
let ok = is_digit(55) && !is_digit(97) && hex_value(97) == 10 && hex_value(70) == 15 && hex_value(103) == 16;
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `hex_value`

```bastio
fn hex_value(c: u8) -> u64
  ensures result <= 16
  ensures is_digit_spec(c) ==> result == c - 48
  ensures result < 16 ==> is_hex_spec(c)
  ensures 97 <= c && c <= 102 ==> result == c - 87
  ensures 65 <= c && c <= 70 ==> result == c - 55
```

The value of a hexadecimal digit (`0-9`, `a-f`, `A-F`), or 16 for any
other byte.

### `parse_u64`

```bastio
fn parse_u64(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> from < to && all_digits(b, from, to) && result.Some == bdec(b, from, to)
```

Bytes `from..to` of `b` as a decimal `u64`: only digits, at least one,
and the value below 2^64. Leading zeros are allowed.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("len=4096");
let mut v = 0;
match parse_u64(b, 4, blen(b)) {
  Option::Some(x) => { v = x; },
  Option::None => {},
}
let bad = parse_u64(b, 0, 3);   // "len" is not a number
bfree(b);
if v != 4096 || bad is Option::Some { return 1; }
```

### `parse_hex_u64`

```bastio
fn parse_hex_u64(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> from < to && all_hex(b, from, to) && result.Some == bhex(b, from, to)
```

Bytes `from..to` of `b` as a hexadecimal `u64` (digits `0-9`, `a-f`,
`A-F`, no `0x` prefix): at least one digit, the value below 2^64.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("dead BEEF");
let a = opt_or[u64](parse_hex_u64(b, 0, 4), 0);
let c = opt_or[u64](parse_hex_u64(b, 5, 9), 0);
bfree(b);
if a != 57005 || c != 48879 { return 1; }
```

### `parse_i64`

```bastio
fn parse_i64(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[i64]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> from < to && dec_signed(b, from, to, result.Some)
```

Bytes `from..to` of `b` as a decimal `i64`: an optional `-`, then digits.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("-42 17");
let mut v: i64 = 0;
match parse_i64(b, 0, 3) {
  Option::Some(x) => { v = x; },
  Option::None => {},
}
let w = opt_or[i64](parse_i64(b, 4, 6), 0);
bfree(b);
if v != -42 || w != 17 { return 1; }
```

### `parse_u32`

```bastio
fn parse_u32(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[u32]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> from < to && all_digits(b, from, to) && result.Some == bdec(b, from, to)
```

`parse_u64`, and the value fits in a `u32`.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("255 256 70000 5000000000");
let a = parse_u8(b, 0, 3);       // fits
let c = parse_u8(b, 4, 7);       // 256 does not fit a u8
let d = parse_u16(b, 8, 13);     // 70000 does not fit a u16
let e = parse_u32(b, 8, 13);     // but fits a u32
let f = parse_u32(b, 14, 24);    // 5000000000 does not
bfree(b);
let ok = a is Option::Some && c is Option::None && d is Option::None && e is Option::Some && f is Option::None;
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `parse_u16`

```bastio
fn parse_u16(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[u16]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> from < to && all_digits(b, from, to) && result.Some == bdec(b, from, to)
```

`parse_u64`, and the value fits in a `u16`.

### `parse_u8`

```bastio
fn parse_u8(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[u8]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> from < to && all_digits(b, from, to) && result.Some == bdec(b, from, to)
```

`parse_u64`, and the value fits in a `u8`.

### `parse_i32`

```bastio
fn parse_i32(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[i32]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> from < to && dec_signed(b, from, to, result.Some)
```

`parse_i64`, and the value fits in an `i32`.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("-128 -129 40000 -2147483648");
let a = parse_i8(b, 0, 4);        // the smallest i8
let c = parse_i8(b, 5, 9);        // one less does not fit
let d = parse_i16(b, 10, 15);     // 40000 does not fit an i16
let e = parse_i32(b, 16, 27);     // the smallest i32
bfree(b);
let ok = a is Option::Some && c is Option::None && d is Option::None && e is Option::Some;
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `parse_i16`

```bastio
fn parse_i16(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[i16]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> from < to && dec_signed(b, from, to, result.Some)
```

`parse_i64`, and the value fits in an `i16`.

### `parse_i8`

```bastio
fn parse_i8(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Option[i8]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> from < to && dec_signed(b, from, to, result.Some)
```

`parse_i64`, and the value fits in an `i8`.

### `dec_digits`

```bastio
fn dec_digits(x: u64) -> u64
  ensures 1 <= result && result <= 20
```

The number of decimal digits of `x`: 1 for 0 to 9, up to 20.

Example:

```bastio
let ok = dec_digits(0) == 1 && dec_digits(9) == 1 && dec_digits(10) == 2 && dec_digits(18446744073709551615) == 20;
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `fmt_u64`

```bastio
fn fmt_u64(t: &mut Vec[u8], x: u64)
  ensures vlen(old(t)) < vlen(t) && vlen(t) <= vlen(old(t)) + 20
  ensures text_digits_from(t, vlen(old(t)))
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends `x` in decimal, with no leading zeros: between 1 and 20 digits.

Example:

```bastio
let mut t = text_new();
text_push_str(&mut t, "pid ");
fmt_u64(&mut t, 4096);
assert vlen(t) > 4;   // at least one digit was appended
text_push(&mut t, 32);
fmt_i64(&mut t, -7);
text_push(&mut t, 32);
fmt_u64_pad(&mut t, 42, 5);
let b = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "pid 4096 -7    42");
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `fmt_u64_pad`

```bastio
fn fmt_u64_pad(t: &mut Vec[u8], x: u64, width: u64)
  ensures vlen(old(t)) < vlen(t)
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends `x` in decimal, padded on the left with spaces to `width` bytes.

### `fmt_i64`

```bastio
fn fmt_i64(t: &mut Vec[u8], x: i64)
  ensures vlen(old(t)) < vlen(t) && vlen(t) <= vlen(old(t)) + 21
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends `x` in decimal, with a `-` in front when it is negative.

### `hex_char`

```bastio
fn hex_char(d: u64) -> u8
  requires d < 16
```

The lowercase hexadecimal digit for `d`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut t = text_new();
fmt_hex_u64(&mut t, 48879, 1);
text_push(&mut t, 32);
fmt_hex_u64(&mut t, 10, 4);   // padded with zeros
text_push(&mut t, hex_char(15));
let b = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "beef 000af");
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `fmt_hex_u64`

```bastio
fn fmt_hex_u64(t: &mut Vec[u8], x: u64, min: u64)
  ensures vlen(old(t)) < vlen(t) && vlen(t) <= vlen(old(t)) + 16
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends `x` in lowercase hexadecimal, without `0x`, using at least
`min` digits (padded with zeros) and at most 16.

### `bytes_put_u64`

```bastio
fn bytes_put_u64(dst: &mut Bytes, at: u64, x: u64) -> u64
  requires at <= blen(dst)
  ensures blen(dst) == blen(old(dst)) && at <= result && result <= blen(dst)
  ensures at < blen(dst) ==> at < result
  ensures forall k: u64 :: at <= k && k < result ==> is_digit_spec(bget(dst, k))
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < blen(dst) && (k < at || k >= result) ==> bget(dst, k) == bget(old(dst), k)
```

Writes `x` in decimal at `at`, as many digits as fit (the leading ones
first). Returns the position after what was written. For a reply built
in a fixed buffer, as a kernel's /proc files are.

Example:

```bastio
let mut o = bfrom("size=......");
let end = bytes_put_u64(&mut o, 5, 1234);
let full = bytes_put_u64(&mut o, blen(o), 7);   // no room: nothing is written
let ok = end == 9 && full == blen(o) && bytes_eq_str(o, "size=1234..");
bfree(o);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

## Specification functions

### `is_digit_spec`

```bastio
spec fn is_digit_spec(c: u8) -> bool {
  48 <= c && c <= 57
}
```

### `is_hex_spec`

```bastio
spec fn is_hex_spec(c: u8) -> bool {
  (48 <= c && c <= 57) || (97 <= c && c <= 102) || (65 <= c && c <= 70)
}
```

### `all_hex`

```bastio
spec fn all_hex(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> bool {
  forall k: u64 :: from <= k && k < to ==> is_hex_spec(bget(b, k))
}
```

Bytes `from..to` of `b` are all hexadecimal digits.

### `all_digits`

```bastio
spec fn all_digits(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> bool {
  forall k: u64 :: from <= k && k < to ==> is_digit_spec(bget(b, k))
}
```

Bytes `from..to` of `b` are all decimal digits.

### `dec_signed`

```bastio
spec fn dec_signed(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64, x: i64) -> bool {
  (bget(b, from) == 45 ==> x == 0 - bdec(b, from + 1, to)) && (bget(b, from) != 45 ==> x == bdec(b, from, to))
}
```

`x` is the value of bytes `from..to` read as a decimal number with an
optional leading `-`.

### `text_digits_from`

```bastio
spec fn text_digits_from(t: &Vec[u8], from: u64) -> bool {
  forall k: u64 :: from <= k && k < vlen(t) ==> is_digit_spec(vget(t, k))
}
```

The new bytes `t[from..]` are all decimal digits.
